chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah be pleased with him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Abū Jaʿfar, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ṣabbāḥ al-Azraq, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said:

Indeed, among the most intense matters the people will face on the Day of qiyamah is that the صاحبُ الخُمُسِ will stand and say: O my Lord, my khums. Yet we have made that lawful for our Shiʿah so that their births may be pure and their children may be purified.

key_terms.الْخُمُسِ: khums, the one-fifth due that belongs by right to its entitled owner
key_terms.شِيعَتِنَا: our Shiʿah, the followers devoted to the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.طَيَّبْنَا: we made lawful or pure for them
key_terms.يَزْكُوَ: to become purified and grow in purity
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection, when people are held to account

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith from al-Istibsar say about khums for the Shiʿah during the ghaybah?
ai.summary: This hadith states that khums is a grave matter connected to accountability on the Day of qiyamah. It also conveys that the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام made it lawful for their Shiʿah in this context so that their lineage and offspring may remain pure.
